title: feat(mcp): read_file extracts PDF and Word text on a bounded worker-thread pool
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9WqhEmMU91L5FoqKXAFQwcE)_
Fixes #31828

Clause-②: no — every `read_file` answer keeps its shape byte for byte (same text, same truncated answer and note at the CPU budget, same retryable over-cap refusal); no new refusal, key, error code or setting.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:AI 助手用 `read_file` 读 PDF / Word 时，文字抽取改在一组工作线程(worker_threads)里跑，池大小就是第一期的并发上限(默认 4),不新增设置;CPU 预算在工作线程内按本线程 CPU 计;超出预算 5 倍墙钟仍没走到检查点的线程被终止并换新，回答已读的页。
- 为什么改:#31100 裁定 B 第二期。第一期只限住了抽取占用请求线程的时长;这一期让请求线程在抽取时照常服务别的请求(实测 1 ms 定时器在抽取期间从 0 次变成约九成照常触发)。
- 风险与回滚：回答形状逐字不变(第一期的用例未改一行全绿);工作线程起不来的宿主(把本包打成单文件的)自动退回进程内抽取并 warn 一次。只动 `@objectstack/mcp`,回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/mcp/src/file-extraction-pool.ts` 的 `runOn`(墙钟上限、终止与替换);`file-content.ts` 的 `withExtractionSlot`(上限拒绝仍在请求线程、先于任何 worker);`tsup.config.ts` 的第二个入口。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`,应见 35 个用例全绿，其中末尾 7 个是新加的工作线程用例。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/mcp/src/file-extraction-pool.ts` (new), the bounded pool:

- **Size = `OS_MCP_READ_FILE_MAX_CONCURRENT`** (phase 1's cap, default 4): one knob, no new variable. The cap itself stays where phase 1 put it, in `withExtractionSlot` on the request thread, checked and taken before the first `await`, so the over-cap refusal (`ReadFileExtractionBusyError`, 503, `retryAfterSeconds`) is decided before any worker is touched and is never queued. Workers start on demand, wait idle (unreferenced, so an idle pool never holds the process open) and are reused.
- **Wall-clock ceiling per job = 5 × the CPU budget** (`READ_FILE_WALL_CEILING_MULTIPLE`, 10 s under the default 2000 ms). Why 5: it is the share of one core a worker still gets when every slot of the default pool (4) and the request thread run on a single core, so a worker still reaching its checkpoints has spent its CPU budget before the ceiling; the ceiling only catches a worker stuck inside one page. Past it the worker is terminated and dropped (never handed another job); the next job starts a fresh one. The answer is built from the pages the worker had streamed back: their text, `truncated: true`, and phase 1's CPU-budget note.
- **Crash**: a worker that emits `error` or exits mid-job is dropped and replaced; its job rejects and `renderReadFile`'s existing net answers phase 1's "The file's content could not be read." No new envelope, no new code.
- **Cannot start** (no built entry beside the module, an entry that throws or exits before it says `ready`, or 10 s without `ready`): extraction runs in-process under phase 1's budget and cap, said once at `warn` naming the reason.
- A worker's stdout is piped to stderr (stdout is the protocol stream on a stdio transport).
- **pdf.js is set up at worker start, not on a job** (round 2): before it says `ready`, a worker loads `unpdf` and reads one page of a built-in one-page PDF (`preloadPdfReader`), which is when pdf.js sets up its in-thread worker and loads the rest of itself. That one-time cost (hundreds of ms on a busy host) is bounded by the 10 s start timeout and is never charged to a job's wall-clock ceiling. Charged to the job (round 1), a small ceiling stopped a cold worker's first read, and the replacement started cold again.

`packages/mcp/src/file-extraction-worker.ts` (new), the worker entry: runs the same `extractDocument` the in-process path runs, streams each PDF page (and each 64-paragraph Word stretch) back as `progress`, and answers `done` / `failed`. Its CPU budget is the worker thread's own clock, `process.threadCpuUsage()` (present on the Node 22 line measured here, 22.23.4), falling back to `performance.eventLoopUtilization().active` where a Node lacks it. `process.cpuUsage()` is not used inside the worker because it counts the whole process. `unpdf` stays a dynamic import (never loaded with the package); the worker loads and sets it up before `ready`.

`packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts`: `extractFileContent` hands PDF and Word jobs to the pool inside the unchanged slot; the extractors gain an optional progress sink, and their answer-building tails moved into `pdfAnswer` / `docxAnswer` so a stopped worker's progress and a finished extraction build the answer through the same code. One deliberate equivalence: `pdfAnswer` sets `truncated` also when a budget note is present; in-process that note only exists when fewer pages than the document has were read, so the in-process answer is unchanged (the phase-1 pins hold it).

`packages/mcp/tsup.config.ts`: a second entry, `src/file-extraction-worker.ts`, so `dist/` carries `file-extraction-worker.js` and `.cjs` beside `index` in both formats. The pool resolves it with `new URL('./file-extraction-worker' + own extension, import.meta.url)`; the CJS build's `import.meta.url` is the existing `shims: true` rewrite. No `exports` change: nothing imports the worker by name. `check-dts-emitted`: 2/2 declared declaration files present.

`content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`: one sentence (extraction runs on worker threads, the server keeps answering).

## Tests

New top-level `describe` at the end of `packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts` (the `read_file` harness). The phase-1 pins are not edited: under vitest the pool's module is the TypeScript source, which has no built worker beside it, so every earlier `describe` runs the in-process fallback, which is phase 1's path. The new `describe` points the pool at the worker's source started through the repo's `tsx` loader (`execArgv: ['--import', tsx]`).

- **CONTROL**: a 3-page PDF and a 2-paragraph `.docx` read in full on a worker; the in-process answers deep-equal the worker answers; the fallback warns once with its reason.
- An entry that throws before `ready` falls back, warns once, answers the same.
- **Event loop keeps ticking**: a 120-page heavy PDF on a warm worker; bound: at least one 1 ms tick per 4 ms of wall and at least 20 (measured in this test: 138/160, 167/188, 173/199 ticks/ms). In-process the count is 0.
- Out of CPU budget on the worker (30 ms): PDF note "after page K of 120", text = pages 1..K; Word note "after N paragraphs" with N a multiple of 64, text = first N paragraphs.
- **Ceiling**: budget 40 ms (ceiling 200 ms), pool of 1, page 2 of 3 alone takes far longer: answer = page 1, `truncated: true`, the exact phase-1 note "after page 1 of 3"; the pool drops the worker (`{ started: 1, idle: 0 }`); the next call is served by a fresh one (`{ started: 2, idle: 1 }`).
- **Crash**: a stand-in worker (data: URL) that exits on a marked file: that call answers the could-not-read sentence, the next is served by a replacement.
- **Over-cap unchanged** with two workers reading: the third call gets the exact phase-1 503 body; both held reads finish in full; both workers return to the pool.

<details><summary>Ablations (mutation landed via scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, red, restored to the HEAD blob; tests import src, no dist leg)</summary>

| # | Mutation (`file-extraction-pool.ts`) | Red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A | `runExtractionInWorker` answers `unavailable` for every job, i.e. extraction back on the request thread | "the request thread keeps ticking…": `expected { ticks: +0, enough: false } to match object { enough: true }`; also CONTROL, fallback-warn, ceiling, crash and over-cap pins (6 failed / 7) |
| B | ceiling path keeps the overrun worker (`settle(false` → `settle(true`), i.e. no replace-on-terminate | "a worker past its wall-clock ceiling…": `expected { started: 1, idle: 1 } to deeply equal { started: 1, idle: +0 }` (1 failed / 7) |

Both legs: `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0`, then `ok restored: blob == HEAD (4b0c78ef2d8d) and git diff HEAD is empty`.
</details>

<details><summary>Measurement (card item 1): 9.21 MiB, 200-page PDF, 2,250 path operators per page, 4-core container; 1 ms setInterval counted during extractFileContent, three runs after one warm-up</summary>

Before, `main` `8079fa9b` (phase 1 landed), default budget:

```
run 1: cpu 326 ms · wall 284 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 284) · text 2890 chars truncated=false
run 2: cpu 288 ms · wall 286 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 286) · text 2890 chars truncated=false
run 3: cpu 318 ms · wall 301 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 301) · text 2890 chars truncated=false
```

After, this branch, the BUILT worker (`dist/file-extraction-worker.js`, then `.cjs`), default budget:

```
esm run 1: wall 248 ms · ticks fired 228 (missed ≈ 20) · text 2890 chars truncated=false
esm run 2: wall 289 ms · ticks fired 262 (missed ≈ 27)
esm run 3: wall 250 ms · ticks fired 224 (missed ≈ 26)
cjs run 1: wall 318 ms · ticks fired 296 (missed ≈ 22)
cjs run 2: wall 332 ms · ticks fired 290 (missed ≈ 42)
cjs run 3: wall 293 ms · ticks fired 268 (missed ≈ 25)
```

Which clock, measured (budget 100 ms): in-process, process CPU stopped the read at 51 / 68 / 83 ms of wall (pages 14 / 46 / 59), because process time also counts V8 helper threads; on the worker, `process.threadCpuUsage()` stopped it at 113 / 107 / 109 ms of wall (pages 25 / 56 / 67) while the request thread fired 95 / 94 / 93 ticks.

Packaging probe, `read_file` through `MCPServerRuntime` imported from the built package, a 120-page heavy PDF: ESM 133 ticks in 162 ms, CJS 196 ticks in 221 ms, no warning (each format found its own worker). With only `index.js` / `index.cjs` copied into a directory with no worker beside them (the bundled-host shape): 0 ticks, the same answer (1690 chars), and one warning naming the missing `file-extraction-worker.js` / `.cjs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Round 2: the ceiling pin red on CI (Test Core 7/8), root cause and repeat runs</summary>

CI on `3d7449c3`: `expected { started: 1, idle: +0 } to deeply equal { started: 1, idle: 1 }` right after the pin's warm-up read. Reproduced locally under CPU contention (6 busy loops on 4 cores): 9 of 10 runs red. A probe of the warm-up answer showed it was killed by the ceiling: `content: none`, "after page 0", 524 ms of wall against a 200 ms ceiling. The cold worker's first PDF paid pdf.js's one-time load and setup inside the job. Loading the `unpdf` module at start alone was not enough (45 of 50 contended runs still red): pdf.js finishes setting itself up on the first document it opens. So the worker now reads one built-in page before `ready`. The assertion is unchanged.

On `1cffd5a8`:

- ceiling pin, 50 runs uncontended: 50 passed, 0 failed
- ceiling pin, 50 runs under 6 busy loops on 4 cores: 50 passed, 0 failed
- the whole worker `describe` (7 pins), 25 runs under the same contention: 25 passed, 0 failed
- ablation B again (keep the overrun worker): red, `expected { started: 1, idle: 1 } to deeply equal { started: 1, idle: +0 }`, restored to the HEAD blob
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- A worker stopped by the ceiling before its PDF opened answers phase 1's empty-text shape (`content: none`, the budget note as the reason) with "after page 0"; after it opened, "after page K of M". Phase 1's in-process path cannot reach the first case (the first page is always read).
- "Cannot start" is recorded for the life of the process (or until `configureExtractionWorkerEntry` / `resetExtractionWorkerPool`, used by tests): a host that could not start the worker once is not retried per call.
- Every worker now loads pdf.js at start, including one that only ever reads Word files (one module load per worker, at most the pool size).
- Workers carry no `resourceLimits`; a worker that runs out of heap is a crash (its call answers could-not-read, the worker is replaced) rather than the process's own out-of-memory. Setting a per-worker heap ceiling is not in this card.
- New names, none exported from the package entry: `READ_FILE_WALL_CEILING_MULTIPLE` (module export in `file-content.ts`), the dist file `file-extraction-worker.{js,cjs}`, and the pool's module exports (`runExtractionInWorker`, `configureExtractionWorkerEntry`, `resetExtractionWorkerPool`, `extractionWorkerPoolStats`).
- `mcp-server-runtime.ts` and `plugin.ts` are untouched: the pool needs no boot wiring (it reads the limits `configureReadFileExtraction` already fixes at `init`).
